quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.
Mirrors are always unreliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles. Check your surroundings, not just your mirrors.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what should you remember?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of large trucks' blind spots. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What should NOT be included in a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: A tire check.
A test of the turn signals.
A paint inspection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A paint inspection.
questions.explanation: Check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands before riding.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle's acceleration and braking change?

options.text: It takes less time to stop and speed up.
It takes the same time to stop and speed up.
It takes more time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle responds more slowly with a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of what material?

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Any soft material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Leather or similar durable materials provide the best grip and protection for riding gloves.

questions.question: How do reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing help riders?

options.text: They should only be worn when riding at night.
They help make motorcycle riders more visible.
They do not increase a rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help make motorcycle riders more visible.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing increases your chances of being seen by other drivers.

questions.question: Who is required to wear a helmet?

options.text: Helmets are not required.
Only motorcycle operators must wear helmets.
Both operators and passengers must wear helmets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both operators and passengers must wear helmets.
questions.explanation: All operators and passengers must wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-compliant helmet.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
You get through the turn faster.
You keep better control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before turning.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A "wobble" is when the front wheel and handlebars shake suddenly. What usually causes this?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
Front wheel not fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble happens when the front wheel and handlebars shake from side to side. This is usually caused by improper weight distribution, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle on the road, how should it be positioned?

options.text: At an angle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb.
Without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking on the road, position your motorcycle at an angle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Check your mirrors only. Look over your shoulder only if something seems wrong.
Either check your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no other vehicles are in your path. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions while riding. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When riding, what type of boots or shoes should you wear?

options.text: Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
Boots or shoes with long heels.
Boots or shoes with long, loose laces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Your footwear should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on level grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is clear pavement at least eight feet wide to the right of the vehicle you are passing. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It severely limits your vision.
It allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
It can be a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people think a helmet limits vision, but this is not true. Any DOT-approved helmet allows you to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: With the front brake only
With the rear brake only
With both brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: With both brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols or letters. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Helps protect your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should maintain a following distance of at least:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Use a larger distance when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the road edge marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: The operator of any motor vehicle involved in a collision resulting in more than $1,000 worth of property damage must:

options.text: File a report, but only if planning to report the accident to their insurance company.
Submit a report of the accident to the DMV.
Contact the highway department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Submit a report of the accident to the DMV.
questions.explanation: You must submit a report to the DMV if your accident causes more than $1,000 in property damage. The DMV can impose penalties if you were in an accident while uninsured.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to adjust to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: In areas where dangers could be present, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Maintain their speed.
Assume they will be safe.
Cover the clutch and both brake levers to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to reduce their reaction time.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, reduce your speed. Keep your hand over the clutch and both brake levers so you can react faster in an emergency.

questions.question: Motorcycles pulling trailers:

options.text: Are not allowed in carpool lanes.
Can travel in any lane on a highway.
Must travel no faster than 25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not allowed in carpool lanes.
questions.explanation: In California, motorcycles towing trailers cannot use carpool lanes. They should stay in the right lane except when passing. Do not drive faster than 55 mph when towing a trailer.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols or letters. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.
